scope: Finite split Brauer tree algebras: connected tree, cyclic orders, at most one exceptional vertex.
methods: Generate bound quiver relations of types I, II, III; omit truncated leaf loops, with the single-edge multiplicity-one exception k[x]/(x^2).
Independently enumerate every string of A/soc(A) modulo inversion. Reachable prefix automaton is checked acyclic; enumerate to exhaustion. Add every explicit indecomposable projective.

Python solves all Hom commutation equations using Gaussian nullspaces over GF(5). For every tested End algebra, all field-linear combinations are enumerated to check nonunit iff diagonal scalar is zero.
Python computes full rad/rad^2 over every intermediate indecomposable, including projectives and nonzero End radicals.

Actual QPA constructs the algebra and all matrix modules; verifies indecomposability, pairwise nonisomorphism, projectivity, injectivity, Jacobson radicals, all Hom dimensions, all irreducible multiplicities, and DTr by unique actual module isomorphism.
JS output is matched to Python modules by actual invertible Hom matrices, then every Hom/Irr entry and every tau target is compared with QPA. No identification by dimension vectors.
nativeQpa137Limitations: BrauerConfigurationAlgebra sorts input cyclic orders in place before constructing arrows; arbitrary ribbon order is not preserved.
BrauerConfigurationAlgebra returns dimension 1 for the single-edge multiplicity-one input; the defined Brauer tree algebra is k[x]/(x^2), dimension 2.
The atlas explicit presentation handles both cases. Native constructor crosschecks were restricted to nondegenerate default-order examples.
